module.geo_data.checks: Locates the target IP address: country, city, provider and autonomous system (ASN).
module.geo_data.fix:
Compare the country, city, hosting provider and ASN shown with what your hosting contract, the region chosen in the provider's console and your legal notice state, then note every difference.
If they differ (other country, other provider), look for the cause in the DNS zone at your DNS manager: an `A` or `AAAA` record left on an old address, an unfinished migration, an intermediate reseller or CDN. Fix the record concerned.
If the address belongs to a CDN or a proxy, the location shown is that of its point of presence, not of the origin server: ask the provider for the real hosting region or read it in its console.
If the site processes personal data of people located in the European Union, check that hosting is in the EU or EEA, or that the transfer is covered (adequacy decision, standard contractual clauses). If in doubt, consult your data protection officer.
Do not take this location as proof: it is approximate (the city can be inexact, the address can be tied to the provider's head office). The reference remains the contract and the region chosen in the console.
Keep an up-to-date inventory (address, provider, ASN, country, date) and rerun the analysis after every migration to spot any drift; the commands in the snippet below show the current address and its location.
module.geo_data.fix_snippet:
# dig
dig +short example.com A
dig +short example.com AAAA

# PowerShell
Resolve-DnsName example.com -Type A
Resolve-DnsName example.com -Type AAAA

# curl
curl -s https://ipinfo.io/203.0.113.10/json
module.geo_data.title: Geolocation
module.geo_data.why: The hosting provider and country matter for compliance (GDPR, data sovereignty) and to understand who operates the infrastructure.
